questions.question: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 3.5 cm, its surface area increases by 550 cm². What was the original radius of the sphere? (use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Difference in **Surface Area** = 4π(R² − r²) = 4π(R − r)(R + r)

Given: R − r = 3.5 cm and Change = 550 cm²

550 = 4 × (22/7) × 3.5 × (2r + 3.5)

550 = 44 × (2r + 3.5) ⇒ 12.5 = 2r + 3.5

2r = 9 ⇒ r = 4.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original radius = **r**

New radius (R) = **r + 3.5 cm**

Increase in Surface Area = **550 cm²**

**Formula Used:**

Surface area of a sphere = **4πr²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43412e4fa8b90e7f7aaa77f53f9eacffab46e92da1641f66ca279922c7060aa0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4πR² − 4πr² = 550

⇒ 4 × (22/7) × [(r + 3.5)² − r²] = 550

⇒ (88/7) × [r² + 7r + 12.25 − r²] = 550

⇒ (88/7) × (7r + 12.25) = 550

⇒ 88 × (r + 1.75) = 550

⇒ r + 1.75 = 550 ÷ 88

⇒ r + 1.75 = 6.25

⇒ r = 6.25 − 1.75 = 4.5

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The volume of a sphere is given by the formula V = (4/3)πr³.

Properties of a Hemisphere

For a hemisphere of radius r, the **Curved Surface Area** is 2πr² and the **Total Surface Area** is 3πr².

Ratio of Surface Areas

If the radii of two spheres are in the ratio a:b, then their surface areas are in the ratio a²:b².</p

questions.question: If p and q are co-primes, then p⁷ and q⁹ are:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If two numbers **p** and **q** are **co-primes**, they share no common prime factors.

Any power of these numbers, such as **p⁷** and **q⁹**, will still only consist of their respective original prime factors.

Since the sets of prime factors remain distinct, **p⁷** and **q⁹** remain **co-primes**.

Because the exponents (7 and 9) are greater than 1, these numbers have more than two factors, making them **composite numbers**.

**∴ The correct answer is co-primes, and composite numbers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **p** and **q** are **co-primes** ⇒ HCF(p, q) = 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/217bb92bf41eebbc9da641bb48225cb342fa7a29c8236bcf8a7604eb8764cd8a.png] 

**Step 1: Analyzing Co-prime Property**

⇒ If p and q share no prime factors, then any power **pⁿ** and **qm** will also share no prime factors.

⇒ Therefore, HCF(p⁷, q⁹) = 1, which means they are **co-primes**.

**Step 2: Analyzing Composite Property**

⇒ A **composite number** is a positive integer greater than 1 that has more than two factors.

⇒ For p⁷, the factors include 1, p, p², p³, p⁴, p⁵, p⁶, and p⁷.

⇒ Since there are more than two factors, **p⁷** and **q⁹** are **composite numbers**.

**∴ The correct answer is co-primes, and composite numbers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are co-prime if their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is 1. Example: (8, 9), (15, 16).

Composite Numbers

Numbers that have more than two factors are called composite numbers. Every **perfect power** nk (where n > 1, k > 1) is always composite.

Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic

Every composite number can be expressed as a unique product of **prime numbers**. If the base primes are different, their powers will never share a common factor.</p

questions.question: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 650 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 8 km and 10.5 km per hour, respectively. The distance (in metres) between them after 12 minutes is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative speed** of the **policeman** = 10.5 − 8 = 2.5 km/h.

Distance covered in 60 min (1 hour) = 2.5 km = 2500 m.

Distance covered in **12 minutes** = 2500 × (12 ÷ 60) = 500 m.

Remaining **distance** between them = 650 − 500 = 150 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 150 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance = 650 m

Speed of **thief** (vₜ) = 8 km/h

Speed of **policeman** (vₚ) = 10.5 km/h

Time (t) = 12 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Same direction) = vₚ − vₜ

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b93a81c1fa6381190a2a0119e28929fe9f874a2d904f4dbb41451c3e0c8a4c6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Relative speed** = 10.5 − 8 = 2.5 km/h

⇒ Converting speed to m/min: 2.5 × (1000 ÷ 60) = 125/3 m/min

⇒ **Distance** reduced in 12 min = (125 ÷ 3) × 12

⇒ Distance reduced = 125 × 4 = 500 m

⇒ **Distance** between them after **12 minutes** = Initial Distance − Distance reduced

⇒ Final distance = 650 − 500 = 150 m

**∴ The correct answer is 150 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the effective speed is the difference: Speed = v₁ − v₂.

Speed Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert km/h to m/min, multiply by 50/3.

Time, Speed, and Distance

Distance = Speed × Time. Always ensure all variables are in consistent units before calculation.</p

questions.question: There are 300 men in a group. They have food for 30 days. After 10 days, 100 more men join the group. Remaining food will last for how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining food duration for **300 men** = 30 − 10 = **20 days**.

Total men after 10 days = 300 + 100 = **400 men**.

Since food is constant, Men × Days = Constant ⇒ 300 × 20 = 400 × New Days.

New Days = 6000 ÷ 400 = **15 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of men (M₁) = **300**

Initial food duration = **30 days**

Time elapsed = **10 days**

Additional men joined = **100**

**Formula Used:**

M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂ (where M is men and D is remaining days)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dcfc878157b6dcf0a7d5dee88d6fb45b89477bfaf83b565e29a473da17702df3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total **food units** initially = 300 × 30 = 9000 man-days.

⇒ Food **consumed** in 10 days = 300 × 10 = 3000 man-days.

⇒ **Remaining food** units = 9000 − 3000 = 6000 man-days.

⇒ Total **new men** (M₂) = 300 + 100 = 400.

⇒ Number of days food will last (D₂) = Remaining Food ÷ M₂

⇒ D₂ = 6000 ÷ 400

⇒ D₂ = 15 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion in Time and Work

The number of days a provision lasts is **inversely proportional** to the number of people. If people increase, the days decrease: M₁/M₂ = D₂/D₁.

Chain Rule Formula

For problems involving men, days, and hours, use (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂, where W is the work or amount of food.

Remaining Provision Logic

Always calculate based on **remaining capacity**. If 'x' days have passed out of 'T' total days, the calculation becomes M₁ × (T − x) = M₂ × Dₙₑw.</p

questions.question: In a seminar. the number of participants in music, physical education and fine arts are 216, 96 and 168, respectively. Find the minimum number of rooms required if each room has the same number of participants and no room has participants from more than one steam seated in it.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To minimize the number of **rooms**, we must maximize the number of **participants** per room.

Max participants per room = **HCF** of 216, 96, and 168.

**HCF**(216, 96, 168) = **24**.

Minimum rooms = (216 + 96 + 168) ÷ 24 = 480 ÷ 24 = **20**.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 rooms.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Participants in **Music** = 216

Participants in **Physical Education** = 96

Participants in **Fine Arts** = 168

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b8e9d3bcf5c77d42cc2cee536162c4e5291ad919fd7c43da48f30751686c35c.png] 

To find the **maximum capacity** of each room:

⇒ Prime factorization of 216 = 2³ × 3³

⇒ Prime factorization of 96 = 2⁵ × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 168 = 2³ × 3 × 7

⇒ **HCF** = 2³ × 3 = 8 × 3 = **24**

Now, calculate the number of rooms for each stream:

⇒ Rooms for **Music** = 216 ÷ 24 = 9

⇒ Rooms for **Physical Education** = 96 ÷ 24 = 4

⇒ Rooms for **Fine Arts** = 168 ÷ 24 = 7

⇒ **Total rooms** = 9 + 4 + 7 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 rooms.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The **HCF** is the largest positive integer that divides each of the integers without a remainder. It is used to find the maximum possible size of identical groups.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The **LCM** is the smallest positive integer that is divisible by all the numbers in a given set. It is used to find common time or meeting points.

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two positive integers a and b, **HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b**.

questions.question: The angle of depression of the foot of a building from the top of a tower 50 m away is 60°. How high is the tower?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°−60°−90°** right-angled triangle, the ratio of sides opposite to these angles is **1 : √3 : 2**.

Here, the distance from the tower (base) is opposite to 30° = **50 m** (1 unit).

The height of the tower is opposite to 60° = **50 × √3 m** (√3 units).

**∴ The correct answer is 50√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

→ **Angle of depression** from the top of the tower = 60°

→ **Horizontal distance** between the tower and the building foot = 50 m

**Formula used:**

→ tan θ = Opposite side ÷ Adjacent side

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/566cdddafadad84780be0fb8f88fba922bda1e7a1ddc0eae7e858c58152e2b74.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **height of the tower** be 'h'.

⇒ The **angle of elevation** from the foot of the building to the top of the tower is also 60° (alternate interior angles).

⇒ In right-angled triangle ABC, tan 60° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ √3 = h ÷ 50

⇒ h = 50 × √3

⇒ h = 50√3 m

⇒ Therefore, the calculated height of the tower corresponds to **Option (3)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 50√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when the object is **below** the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Values for Heights

Common values: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Relationship of Angles

Angle of elevation is always **numerically equal** to the angle of depression when measured between the same two points.</p

questions.question: The interest of (10r)² in r time at rate (r)/(10)% is __________.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert **Principal**: P = (10r)² = 100r².

Total Interest Percentage = **Rate** × **Time** = (r/10)% × r = r²/10%.

**Simple Interest** = Principal × Total Interest % = 100r² × (r²/10)/100.

SI = (100r² × r²) ÷ 1000 = 100r⁴ ÷ 1000 = r⁴/10.

**∴ The correct answer is r⁴/10.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Principal (P)** = (10r)² = 100r²

⇒ **Time (T)** = r

⇒ **Rate (R)** = r/10 %

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab4c7b11ec229680d20e441950dabe86a2c27b5203783dc23f4de24e983a4736.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (100r² × (r/10) × r) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (100r² × r²/10) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (10r⁴) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = r⁴/10

**∴ The correct answer is r⁴/10.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

It is the interest calculated only on the **Principal** amount for the entire duration: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Total Amount (A)

The total sum of money returned after the given time period, calculated as Amount = Principal + Interest.

Effective Rate of Interest

For a simple interest scenario, the **Effective Interest Rate** over the total duration is simply (Rate × Time)%.</p

questions.question: Find the altitude (in cm) of side MT of triangle MNT with side MN = 36 cm, MT = 36 cm and NT = 48 cm.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In isosceles ΔMNT, the altitude to the unequal side NT (48 cm) bisects it into two 24 cm segments.

Height to side NT = √(36² − 24²) = √720 = 12√5 cm.

Area of ΔMNT = 1/2 × 48 × 12√5 = 288√5 cm².

Equating area for base MT: 1/2 × 36 × Altitude = 288√5 cm².

Altitude to MT = (288√5 × 2) ÷ 36 = 16√5 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 16√5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides of ΔMNT: MN = 36 cm, MT = 36 cm, and NT = 48 cm.

questions.question: The salaries of P and Q together amount to Rs. 6,40,000. P and Q save 60% and 40%, respectively, of their individual salaries. If their expenditures are the same, then what is the ratio of P's salary to Q's salary?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Expenditure %** of P = 100% − 60% = 40%

**Expenditure %** of Q = 100% − 40% = 60%

Given: Expenditure of P = Expenditure of Q

⇒ 40% of **Salary P** = 60% of **Salary Q**

⇒ Salary P / Salary Q = 60 / 40 = 3 / 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Salary (P + Q) = ₹6,40,000

Savings of P = 60% | Savings of Q = 40%

Expenditure of P = Expenditure of Q

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78d9403b3de26ed6ac7a294c5d3c6f49e4392c73167a2d504314b0212260c999.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let P be the salary of P and Q be the salary of Q.

⇒ Expenditure of P = 100% − Savings % = 100% − 60% = 40% of P

⇒ Expenditure of Q = 100% − Savings % = 100% − 40% = 60% of Q

⇒ According to the question: 40% × P = 60% × Q

⇒ (40/100) × P = (60/100) × Q

⇒ 40 × P = 60 × Q

⇒ P / Q = 60 / 40

⇒ P / Q = 3 / 2

⇒ **Ratio** = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income Formula

Total Income is always the sum of Expenditure and Savings: **Income = Expenditure + Savings**.

Percentage Expenditure

If a person saves x% of their income, then their expenditure percentage is **(100 − x)%** of the total income.

Ratio of Quantities

When a% of A equals b% of B, the ratio A : B is always the inverse of the percentage coefficients: **A : B = b : a**.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 3⁸ is divided by 7?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using Fermat's Little Theorem: ap−¹ ≡ 1 (mod p) for any prime p.

Here p = 7, so 3⁶ ≡ 1 (mod 7).

We can write 3⁸ = 3⁶ × 3².

So, 3⁸ ≡ 1 × 9 ≡ 9 (mod 7).

When 9 is divided by 7, the remainder is 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 3⁸ ÷ 7

**Concept Used:**

Properties of remainders: (A × B) mod N = [(A mod N) × (B mod N)] mod N

**Calculation:**

⇒ The given expression 3⁸ can be written as (3²)⁴.

⇒ (3²)⁴ = 9⁴

⇒ Find the remainder when the base 9 is divided by 7.

⇒ 9 ÷ 7 leaves a remainder of 2.

⇒ Now, replace 9 with its remainder in the original power expression: 2⁴

⇒ 2⁴ = 16

⇒ Finally, divide 16 by 7 to get the final remainder.

⇒ 16 = 7 × 2 + 2

⇒ The remainder is 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fermat's Little Theorem

It states that if p is a prime number, then for any integer a, the number ap−¹ − 1 is an integer multiple of p. The formula is expressed as ap−¹ ≡ 1 (mod p).

Euler's Totient Theorem

It generalizes Fermat's theorem, stating aφ⁽ⁿ⁾ ≡ 1 (mod n) where a and n are coprime, and φ(n) represents Euler's totient function.

Successive Squaring Concept

Large powers can be calculated efficiently by repeatedly squaring the base and taking the remainder at each step to keep the numbers small and manageable.
</p

In what ratio, wheat at ₹23 per kg should be mixed with wheat at ₹14 per kg so that on selling the mixture at ₹20 per kg there is a profit of 25%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of the mixture = 20 × (100 ÷ 125) = ₹16 per kg.

By alligation rule, Ratio = (16 − 14) ∶ (23 − 16) = 2 ∶ 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ∶ 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price of 1st variety of wheat = ₹23/kg

Price of 2ⁿd variety of wheat = ₹14/kg

Selling Price (SP) of the mixture = ₹20/kg

Profit = 25%

**Formula Used:**

CP = SP × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)]

Quantity 1 / Quantity 2 = (Mean CP − Price 2) / (Price 1 − Mean CP)

questions.question: Two triangles Δ ABC and Δ DEF are similar. If AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm and DE = 9 cm, find EF.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **similar triangles** ΔABC and ΔDEF, the **ratio of corresponding sides** is equal.

Side Ratio: AB ÷ DE = BC ÷ EF

Substitute values: 6 ÷ 9 = 8 ÷ EF

2 ÷ 3 = 8 ÷ EF

EF = (8 × 3) ÷ 2 = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm, DE = 9 cm, and ΔABC ∼ ΔDEF.

**Formula Used:** Ratio of corresponding sides of similar triangles: AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a10905055c267658a7b164e60862a217840e8b506e325a8026168ab862edcfa.png] 

Since ΔABC ∼ ΔDEF, we use the property of proportionality:

⇒ AB ÷ DE = BC ÷ EF

⇒ 6 ÷ 9 = 8 ÷ EF

⇒ 2 ÷ 3 = 8 ÷ EF

⇒ 2 × EF = 8 × 3

⇒ 2 × EF = 24

⇒ EF = 24 ÷ 2

⇒ EF = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

AA (Angle-Angle) Similarity

If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another triangle, then the two triangles are similar.

Area Ratio Property

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(Δ1)/Area(Δ2) = (Side1/Side2)².

Corresponding Parts

In similar triangles, corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio (proportional).</p

questions.question: In society A, the number of females is 250 and 50% of its total population are males. In society B, the number of males is 900 and 40% of its total population are females. What is the percentage of females in society B with respect to the total population of society A?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Society A**: 50% (Females) = 250 ⇒ 100% (Total A) = 500

**Society B**: 60% (Males) = 900 ⇒ 40% (Females B) = (900 ÷ 60) × 40 = 600

Required % = (Females in B ÷ Total A) × 100 = (600 ÷ 500) × 100 = 120%

**∴ The correct answer is 120%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In **Society A**: Females = 250, Males = 50% of total.

In **Society B**: Males = 900, Females = 40% of total.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/65c6d03ac2f678f67deb6f8902dd3492aae0f7eb7f55e5185c88f9693795987e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total population** of **society A**: Since 50% are males, 50% must be females. 50% = 250 ⇒ Total = (250 ÷ 50) × 100 = 500

⇒ In **society B**, percentage of males = 100% − 40% = 60%

⇒ **Total population** of **society B**: 60% = 900 ⇒ Total = (900 ÷ 60) × 100 = 1500

⇒ Number of **females** in **society B** = 40% of 1500 = (40 ÷ 100) × 1500 = 600

⇒ Required percentage = (Females in B ÷ Total Population in A) × 100

⇒ Required percentage = (600 ÷ 500) × 100 = 1.2 × 100 = 120%

**∴ The correct answer is 120%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage with respect to a base

To find the percentage of value X with respect to Y, use the formula: (X ÷ Y) × 100. Here, Y is the base value.

Total from Percentage

If P% of a value is V, then the total value is calculated as V × (100 ÷ P).

Complementary Percentages

In a population consisting of two groups (e.g., males and females), if one group is X%, the other is (100 − X)%.</p

questions.question: Which of the following three-dimensional geometric figures has eight vertices and six rectangular faces?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the shape based on its **structural properties**:

A **Cuboid** (also known as a rectangular prism) uniquely possesses **6 rectangular faces**.

Number of **vertices** (corners) in a cuboid = 8 (4 at the top + 4 at the bottom).

Number of **edges** (lines) = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is Cuboid.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Number of **faces** = 6 (all are **rectangles**).

⇒ Number of **vertices** = 8.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78bc09d22db2632b4bc0ec4362383f115bed49c5edaa710ba9d4b73d535e5ec0.png] 

**Verification using Properties:**

⇒ A **Pyramid** (Square-based) has 5 vertices and 5 faces.

⇒ A **Cylinder** has 0 vertices and 3 surfaces (not all rectangular).

⇒ A **Parallelogram** is a 2D figure, not a 3D geometric solid.

⇒ A **Cuboid** satisfies the condition of having **8 vertices** and **6 rectangular faces**.

**∴ The correct answer is Cuboid.**

**__Additional Information__**

Euler's Formula

For any polyhedron, the number of Faces (F), Vertices (V), and Edges (E) are related by: F + V − E = 2.

Cube vs Cuboid

A **Cube** is a special type of cuboid where all **6 faces** are **equal squares**. Both have 8 vertices and 12 edges.

Volume and Surface Area

For a cuboid with length (l), breadth (b), and height (h): Volume = l × b × h and Total Surface Area = 2(lb + bh + hl).</p

questions.question: Akshay gets 2% increase in his sale amount in the first year and 25% in the second year. With that his present sale is ₹1,42,800. What was his sale (in ₹) two years ago?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Ratio Method** for successive percentage increases:

Year 1 increase (2%) → 1/50 (Ratio: 50 → 51)

Year 2 increase (25%) → 1/4 (Ratio: 4 → 5)

Net Ratio = (50 × 4) : (51 × 5) = 200 : 255

Given: 255 units = ₹1,42,800 ⇒ 1 unit = 1,42,800 ÷ 255 = 560

Initial Sale (200 units) = 200 × 560 = ₹1,12,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,12,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present Sale = **₹1,42,800**

First year increase = **2%**

Second year increase = **25%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b0d77afef4dd1626e3d8ddd704cf3a5b4f69fd721637f7ba46877cda8546b2d.png] 

Let the sale two years ago be **X**.

⇒ Final Sale = Initial Sale × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100)

⇒ 1,42,800 = X × (1 + 2/100) × (1 + 25/100)

⇒ 1,42,800 = X × (102/100) × (125/100)

⇒ 1,42,800 = X × (51/50) × (5/4)

⇒ 1,42,800 = X × (255/200)

⇒ X = (1,42,800 × 200) ÷ 255

⇒ X = 560 × 200

⇒ X = 1,12,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,12,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net effective change is (a + b + ab/100)%.

Reverse Calculation Trick

Initial Value = Final Value × [100/(100 + r₁)] × [100/(100 + r₂)]. This is useful for finding original prices/amounts.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

2% = 1/50, 25% = 1/4, 20% = 1/5, 10% = 1/10. Fractions simplify large multiplication and division steps.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks up his goods by 30% and then gives a discount of 10% on the marked price. Apart from this, he uses a faulty balance which reads 1 kg for 870 g. What is his net profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Multiplier = (**Markup Factor**) × (**Discount Factor**) × (**Weight Factor**)

Net Multiplier = (130 / 100) × (90 / 100) × (1000 / 870)

Net Multiplier = 1.3 × 0.9 × (100 / 87) = 1.17 × (100 / 87) = 117 / 87 = 39 / 29

Profit % = [(39 − 29) / 29] × 100 = (10 / 29) × 100 ≈ 34.48%

**∴ The correct answer is 34.48%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Markup** = 30%, **Discount** = 10%, **Faulty weight** = 870 g instead of 1000 g.

**Formula Used:**

Net Profit % = [(Total SP / Total CP) − 1] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/819023e39fe0f72c1f6f9700fdcca510fa4e9779b78b0e9876db0273bb152c77.png] 

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 g of goods be ₹1.

⇒ **Actual CP** for the shopkeeper (for 870 g) = 870 × 1 = ₹870.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** for 1000 g = 1000 + 30% of 1000 = ₹1300.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** after 10% discount on MP = 1300 − (10 / 100) × 1300.

⇒ **SP** = 1300 − 130 = ₹1170.

⇒ **Net Profit** = SP − CP = 1170 − 870 = ₹300.

⇒ **Net Profit %** = (300 / 870) × 100.

⇒ **Net Profit %** = (30 / 87) × 100 = (10 / 29) × 100 ≈ 34.48%.

**∴ The correct answer is 34.48%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

Profit % due to weight fraud = [True Value − False Value] / False Value × 100. In this case, (1000 − 870) / 870 × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Relationship: SP = CP × (1 + Markup %) × (1 − Discount %). This represents the **price multiplier** effect.

Successive Percentage Change

The effective percentage change for two successive changes x% and y% is [x + y + (xy / 100)]%.

questions.question: If the product of zeros of the polynomial f(x) = ax³ + 4x² - 2x - 6 is 2, then the value of 'a' =
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For any cubic polynomial, the **product of zeroes** is given by the formula: −d/a.

Comparing with the given polynomial f(x) = ax³ + 4x² − 2x − 6, we have the constant term d = −6.

Product of zeroes = −(−6) ÷ a = 6/a.

Given that the product is 2 ⇒ 6/a = 2 ⇒ a = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The polynomial is f(x) = ax³ + 4x² − 2x − 6.

The **product of zeroes** of this polynomial is 2.

**Formula Used:**

For a standard cubic polynomial of the form f(x) = Ax³ + Bx² + Cx + D, the **product of its zeroes** (αβγ) is given by:

αβγ = −D/A = −(constant term) ÷ (coefficient of x³)

**Calculations:**

Comparing the given polynomial f(x) = ax³ + 4x² − 2x − 6 with the standard cubic form:

⇒ A = a

⇒ B = 4

⇒ C = −2

⇒ D = −6

Now, substitute these coefficients into the product of zeroes formula:

⇒ Product of zeroes = −(−6) ÷ a

⇒ 2 = 6/a

⇒ 2 × a = 6

⇒ a = 3

Thus, the value of the coefficient 'a' is 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cubic Polynomial Relations

For a cubic polynomial f(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d with roots α, β, and γ, the relations are: Sum of roots = −b/a, Sum of products taken two at a time = c/a, and Product of roots = −d/a.

Quadratic Polynomial Relations

For a quadratic polynomial f(x) = ax² + bx + c with roots α and β, the relations are: Sum of roots = −b/a, and Product of roots = c/a.

General Polynomial Root Product

For any nth-degree polynomial, the product of all roots is given by (−1)ⁿ × (constant term) ÷ (leading coefficient).</p

questions.question: For a given circle of radius 4 cm, the angle of its sector is 45º. Find the area (in cm²) of the sector. (Use π = 3.14.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

An angle of **45°** represents exactly **1/8** of the total **360°** circle area.

Total Area of Circle = πr² = 3.14 × 4² = 3.14 × 16 = 50.24 cm².

Area of Sector = Total Area ÷ 8

Area of Sector = 50.24 ÷ 8 = 6.28 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 6.28 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius (r)** of the circle = 4 cm

**Sector angle (θ)** = 45°

**π** = 3.14

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/379934a768560ed526de1fba1898e0df37955aa9faed77bbbd4b6a95182b4a0b.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Area of a Sector = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = (45 ÷ 360) × 3.14 × (4)²

⇒ Area = (1 ÷ 8) × 3.14 × 16

⇒ Area = (16 ÷ 8) × 3.14

⇒ Area = 2 × 3.14

⇒ Area = 6.28 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 6.28 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Length of an Arc

The distance along the curved boundary of the sector is calculated as L = (θ ÷ 360) × 2πr.

Perimeter of a Sector

The total boundary length of the sector is equal to the arc length plus two radii: P = L + 2r.

Area in terms of Arc Length

If the length of the arc (L) is known, the area of the sector can be written as Area = (1 ÷ 2) × L × r.

Area of a Segment

The area of the segment is the sector area minus the area of the triangle formed by the radii and the chord: Area = Sector Area − (1 ÷ 2)r² sin(θ).</p

questions.question: 450 candidates apply for admission in a school. 10% candidates being Over Age do not give the exam and 20% fail in the exam. How many candidates will qualify for admission?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **successive percentage** reduction method.

Qualified candidates = **Total** × (100 − **OverAge %**) × (100 − **Fail %**)

Qualified candidates = 450 × 90% × 80%

Qualified candidates = 450 × 0.9 × 0.8 = 450 × 0.72 = 324

**∴ The correct answer is 324.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **candidates** applied = 450

**Over age** candidates = 10%

**Failed** candidates = 20% of those who took the exam.

 
 
 Total Candidates = 450
 
 
 
 
 10% (45)
 Over Age
 Appeared = 405 (90%)
 
 
 
• 
 
 
 20% (81)
 Qualified = 324 (80%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of **over age** candidates = 10% of 450

⇒ Over age candidates = (10 ÷ 100) × 450 = 45

⇒ Candidates who **appeared** for the exam = 450 − 45 = 405

⇒ Number of candidates who **failed** = 20% of 405

⇒ Failed candidates = (20 ÷ 100) × 405 = 81

⇒ Number of candidates who **qualified** = 405 − 81

⇒ Qualified candidates = 324

**∴ The correct answer is 324.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by a% and then by b%, the net effective change is given by [a + b + (ab ÷ 100)]%.

Base Value Concept

Always identify the correct base for percentage calculation; here, the failure percentage is calculated on the number of candidates who actually appeared, not the original total.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

10% = 1/10 and 20% = 1/5. Using fractions can often speed up calculations in competitive exams.</p
